**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Separate calls when an indexed slot has a different ID.**

When Ollama emits two distinct tool calls with `index: 0`, this return routes both calls to the same accumulator. The second call replaces the first call’s ID and name. Their arguments concatenate, so JSON parsing falls back to `{}`. Ollama documents this emitted shape. Resolve an occupied-index conflict by call ID before reusing the slot, and add a regression case with two distinct IDs at index 0. ([github.com](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/15497?utm_source=openai))

**🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Record a later index when a known ID rejoins its slot.**

If the first delta for `call_a` has no index, a later delta with `id: "call_a"` and `index: 0` returns here without recording index 0. A subsequent anonymous fragment with `index: 0` then starts a second slot. The original call loses that argument fragment and can execute with empty parameters. Update the matched entry’s index when one becomes available, and cover this sequence in a regression test.

Good catch, thanks. The slot was taken from the index alone, so two calls with different ids at index 0 (what Ollama sends, see ollama/ollama#15497) shared a slot: the second overwrote the id and name, and the arguments were joined into invalid JSON.

The new commit opens a new slot when the index is already used by a call with another id, and reuses it when the id matches. A later fragment that has an index but no id continues the latest call that used that index. Calls that arrive with a distinct index per call behave as before.

Two regression tests were added to `tests/test_pipeline_openai_adapters.py`: two distinct ids at index 0, and a fragment without an id continuing the second of them. Both fail on the previous commit and pass now, together with the existing tests in that file.
